items.title: US military disables commercial bulk carrier attempting to cross Iran blockade
items.summary: US Central Command says it disabled the St Kitts and Nevis-flagged bulk carrier Huda in the Gulf of Oman on November 7 after repeated warnings during an attempted departure following a visit to an Iranian port. This is a material escalation in direct enforcement of the US maritime blockade. The event does not establish an additional oil-supply outage; monitor retaliatory action, ship routing and insurance costs.

items.title: Tanker fire near Khasab prompts crew evacuation amid persistent Hormuz shipping risk
items.summary: UKMTO Warning 199-26 reports a tanker on fire approximately eight nautical miles northwest of Khasab, Oman, on November 7; military authorities reported that the crew evacuated. The warning was issued on November 8 as a delayed report. The cause, vessel identity, casualties, pollution and any additional oil-throughput loss are not confirmed; avoid attributing the fire to a particular belligerent without evidence.

items.key_finding: A new tanker evacuation demonstrates ongoing acute vessel risk near Hormuz, but does not establish a new oil-volume shock.

items.title: Berkshire increases quarterly repurchases to $9.6 billion despite lower operating profit
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway reported a nearly six-percent year-over-year decline in quarterly operating earnings, driven partly by weaker insurance underwriting, while spending $9.6 billion on share repurchases. Its railroad and utility businesses delivered stronger results. The large capital-return commitment is a defensive-sector watch-list signal, but Monday's price response is not yet observable.

items.title: New US strikes on Qeshm Island raise Hormuz escalation risk
items.summary: President Trump said US forces struck an Iranian air-defense installation on Qeshm Island on November 6; Iranian state media separately reported explosions nearby. The announcement raises the risk of retaliation around a major shipping chokepoint. No additional tanker damage, lost petroleum throughput or post-event market reaction has been independently verified.

items.title: Qatari two-day framework proposes reopening Hormuz, but remains unsigned
items.summary: Regional officials describe a two-day diplomatic proposal involving US blockade relief and partial release of Iranian assets in exchange for access by international nuclear inspectors. Iran would reopen Hormuz on the second day through a route negotiated with Oman. Iran's additional demands remain unresolved, and no restoration of physical tanker traffic has been verified.
